artifact.self_contained_problem:
A finite point set $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ is said to be in general position if no three points of $P$ are collinear and no four points of $P$ are cocircular. For a finite set $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$, let $d(P)=|\{\|p-q\|:p,q\in P,\,p\ne q\}|$ denote the number of distinct pairwise Euclidean distances determined by $P$. Define
$$D_{\mathrm{gen}}(n)=\min\{d(P):P\subset\mathbb{R}^2,\ |P|=n,\ P\text{ in general position}\}.$$
It is known that $D_{\mathrm{gen}}(n)=\Omega(n)$ and that $D_{\mathrm{gen}}(n)\le n\cdot 2^{O(\sqrt{\log n})}$. Determine the asymptotic order of $D_{\mathrm{gen}}(n)$ as $n\to\infty$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of determining the asymptotics of the minimum number of distinct distances among n planar points in general position (no 3 collinear, no 4 cocircular) appears to remain open. Best known bounds are Ω(n) lower and n·2^{O(√log n)} upper; no improvement closing the gap was located in the search.

status_evidence.title: Distinct Distances: Open Problems and Current Bounds
status_evidence.snippet: Problem 8. Find the asymptotic value of D_gen(n). D_gen(n) ≥ Ω(n) and a construction gives D_gen(n) ≤ n·2^{O(√log n)}.
status_evidence.claim: The asymptotic value of D_gen(n) is listed as an open problem with these bounds.

status_evidence.title: Points in General Position — Some Plane Truths
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of distinct distances for points in general position; the problem of closing the gap remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent expository sources continue to describe the asymptotic of D_gen(n) as an open problem.
